\paragraph{Relation to prior work.} White-box probes read deception from activations~\citep{zou2023representation, burns2022discovering, azaria2023internal}; the black-box line's closest instance---our primary audit target---is \citet{pacchiardi2024catch}, and we audit both paradigms (§\ref{sec:td_vs_fd}). Three concurrent evaluations~\citep{kretschmar2025liarsbench, cooney2026didyoulie, hopkins2026liedetectors} find lie detectors fail to \textbf{generalize} beyond the regime they were fit in. That is a question about \textbf{predictive validity}; ours is the prior one, about \textbf{attributional validity}: instructed-lie accuracy is \textbf{not merely poorly generalizing but uninterpretable as evidence about deception}, because the intervention moves deception and compliance together---so generalization can be perfect while identification still fails. \textbf{Fixed elicitation is also not what we claim to introduce}---\citet{cooney2026didyoulie}'s trained organisms have it and go \emph{beyond} it, with $D$ \emph{set} rather than observed. \textbf{Our novelty is using it as the missing construct-validity criterion for reading instructed-benchmark accuracy}: we formalize the identification failure, turn it into an auditable protocol, and \textbf{show empirically that the confound accounts for substantial benchmark accuracy across three mechanistically distinct detector paradigms}---while auditing whether public artifacts supply the criterion at all. Appendix~\ref{app:related_work} places all five kinds against requirements~(i)--(v) (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:prior_work_criteria}).

\paragraph{Intervals on the pre-registered panel.} Wilson 95\% intervals ($n\!=\!50$ per cell), instructed against equalized, in table order and in percent: Llama~3.2~3B [92.9, 100.0] against [14.3, 37.4]; Llama~3.1~8B [73.8, 93.0] against [29.4, 55.8]; Mistral~7B [92.9, 100.0] against [44.2, 70.6]; Qwen~2.5~7B [92.9, 100.0] against [36.6, 63.4]; Qwen~2.5~14B [92.9, 100.0] against [33.0, 59.6]; Qwen~2.5~32B [92.9, 100.0] against [29.4, 55.8]; pooled ($n\!=\!300$) \textbf{[94.4, 98.4] against [37.8, 49.0]}. \textbf{All six instructed intervals exclude chance and five of six equalized intervals contain it}, and the pooled pair is \textbf{45.4\,pp apart at its nearest edges}, so the collapse is a statement about two intervals that do not approach one another rather than about two point estimates.

\paragraph{The sixth equalized interval, and why the estimator matters.} Llama~3.2~3B's equalized interval, [14.3, 37.4], excludes chance from \emph{below}, which read alone would suggest inverted discrimination. It does not, and the reason is the unit. Each cell's 50 trials come from \textbf{25 matched claim pairs}, two rows apiece, so the pair rather than the trial is the inferential unit; a cluster bootstrap over pairs (2{,}000 draws, \texttt{SEED}=42, each drawn copy given a fresh group id so that \texttt{GroupKFold} cannot place a duplicated pair in both a training and a test fold) puts that cell at \textbf{[34.0, 70.0]}, which contains chance. That is the caveat Figure~\ref{fig:r1c_collapse} already states in words, now with an interval attached. \textbf{The clustered intervals are on the \texttt{grp-5f} column and not on the primary, and that is forced rather than chosen}: resampling pairs duplicates rows, under stratified folds a duplicated row is trained on and then scored, and in a first pass that leakage inflated every draw enough that the interval failed to contain its own point estimate. Across all 28 cells of both panels, every clustered interval contains its grouped point estimate.

\paragraph{The pooled digit carries row-order noise, and we found that by computing these intervals.} All 24 per-target cells recompute to their published literals exactly. The four \emph{pooled} cells do so only when the six targets are stacked in the order the publishing script pooled them, alphabetical by checkpoint filename; stacking them in the order these two tables print their rows gives 80.3\% and 49.3\% on the v1 panel and 96.7\% and 44.3\% here, from the same rows under the same estimator. The cause is not an unfixed seed but \texttt{StratifiedKFold(shuffle=True, random\_state=0)}, whose fold assignment is a function of a row's position in the stacked matrix, so reordering the per-target blocks reshuffles which rows share a fold. \textbf{Every one of those four swings, 0.3 to 4.3\,pp, lies inside the Wilson interval for its own cell}, which is precisely the argument for reporting an interval: a pooled point estimate carrying a few pp of row-order noise is a number that should never have been printed bare. No per-target cell, no permutation $p$, no change in pp and no verdict moves, and the collapse survives either ordering with the instructed and equalized intervals still disjoint. Recomputed by \texttt{experiments/analyze\_r1\_intervals.py}, which pins the six-target roster (the \texttt{r1b\_fresh} glob now also matches \texttt{ministral-3:8b}, an EXP-R1d target collected after this panel was published, whose inclusion would give $n\!=\!350$) and asserts every cell's point accuracy equals its published table literal before emitting any interval, with no model call and no network access.

\textbf{The T/D vs.\ F/D contrast} (Table~\ref{tab:td_vs_fd}) is the one contrast in the design that lies \emph{within} a single instructed-deception condition---both cells carry the same complied-with instruction and the benchmark labels them identically. It does \textbf{not} establish that latent $D$ is fixed: $D$ is never observed (§\ref{sec:identification}), and the corrective leakage documented below shows that compliance is graded rather than binary. It is paired at the level of the matched claim pair, so claim-level variation is removed; the permutation test ($B\!=\!10{,}000$, seed 42) flips the T/D-vs-F/D assignment within each pair, and detector-score differences are standardized by the SD of that panel's own outcome for comparability with the $\beta$ estimates of §\ref{sec:factorial} (\texttt{analyze\_factorial\_td\_vs\_fd.py}). Both panels move within the condition. The marker's shift is significant on Qwen~2.5~14B only, where the RC$\geq$1 fire rate is 62\% against 6\% with non-overlapping Wilson intervals; the complete detector's shift is significant on two of three targets and \emph{oppositely signed} between them, at magnitudes ($-1.37$, $+1.61$\,SD) comparable to the instruction main effect. Because the contrast varies truth-value together with how hard the assigned argument is to comply with, it does not identify which of the two the detectors read. What it does establish is that detector output varies by more than the instruction main effect \emph{inside} a condition the benchmark treats as a single ground-truth class: either a large part of the signal is not deception, or deception itself varies within the class---and on either reading the instruction is not the ground truth the benchmark takes it for. Note also that $S$ has $V$ and $B$ as further parents (Figure~\ref{fig:dag}), so a truth-value effect could produce this movement while leaving a genuine $D\!\to\!S$ component intact; that possibility is not excluded here.

\paragraph{What is not measured in either instructed cell, and the one measurement that would settle it.} \textbf{No grade of $D$ exists for any response in T/D or F/D.} Both cells are defined by the instruction issued, compliance is inferred from it, and the statement above that compliance is \emph{graded rather than binary} is read off corrective leakage in the detector's own features, not off any per-response judgment of whether the answer asserts something the target does not hold. That is why this contrast is reported as non-identifying rather than as evidence. \textbf{The measurement that would settle how graded compliance is} is a per-response deception grade on these outputs, blind to cell and to target, of the kind §\ref{app:crit4_ours} runs for EXP-C4: it would convert the qualitative claim into a rate, and a T/D cell whose responses were frequently \emph{not} deceptive would show directly that the benchmark's instructed label is not a deception label. That coding sheet is prepared and released (\texttt{make\_factorial\_coding\_sheet.py}; 144 items, 12 per (target,~cell), globally shuffled at seed 42), and it interleaves \emph{all four} cells rather than T/D with F/D alone. The reason is that within \{T/D,~F/D\} the instruction is constant, so blinding on it would be vacuous, while the truth-value cannot be blinded at all from a coder who knows that water boils at $100^\circ$C. What can be withheld is the target's identity and whether a deception instruction was issued, and withholding the latter requires the honest cells in the pool; they also supply the control rate a T/D rate needs. The item-to-condition key is held in a separate file, and no response in the sheet names its own instruction (measured; the one keyword hit is the phrase ``genetic instructions''), so the blind survives the response text as well as the layout. \textbf{No rate from it is reported here}: hand-coding is the protocol §\ref{app:crit4_ours} uses, and substituting a machine grade would be the exact failure this paper names as construct recovery, in the one place where it would matter most.

Deception-related information is encoded in model activations and extractable with weight access---honesty/deception directions~\citep{zou2023representation}, unsupervised truthfulness probes~\citep{burns2022discovering}, activation classifiers (SAPLMA;~\citealp{azaria2023internal}), inference-time steering (ITI;~\citealp{li2023inference})---all requiring access unavailable for API-only models. Unlike externally induced misbehavior~\citep{goodfellow2014explaining, perez2022ignore}, the model itself is the source of the deceptive output here.
